Definition: from G394 (like G331, but in a good sense); a votive offering:--gift.
BiblicalUsage: Luke records this word once, where some speak of the temple adorned with goodly stones and gifts. Here it means a votive offering, something dedicated and set out in honour of God, the opposite sense of the curse-word that shares its spelling.
TheologicalSignificance: A single mention of temple gifts holds no teaching of its own; what matters is the contrast, that the same root can name a gift given to God or a person cut off from Him.
